source.title: Effects of water and temperature on reaction mechanism and crystal properties in a reactive crystallization of paracetamol
source.journal: Chemical Engineering and Processing - Process Intensification
source.evidence_accessed: Publisher highlights and abstract; detailed methods and numerical tables were not accessed.

reported_comparison.condition: water present, within the authors' reported process
reported_comparison.observation: Paracetamol form I particles with high purity (99%) reported.
reported_comparison.measurement_basis: Product purity as stated in abstract; not isolated yield or individual impurity concentration.
reported_comparison.does_not_establish: Zero 4-acetoxyacetanilide formation, a universal water threshold, safe residual concentration, or transferability to arbitrary routes.

reported_comparison.condition: water absent, within the authors' reported process
reported_comparison.does_not_establish: Formation or quantity in any locally generated route.

identified_alternative_product.name: 4-acetoxyacetanilide
identified_alternative_product.role_in_our_work: Literature-grounded candidate requiring recipe matching; not an observed local product, stoichiometric coproduct, or automatic prediction.

controls_and_missing_evidence.comparative_control: Water-present versus water-absent conditions are reported, but the abstract does not establish a zero-byproduct negative control.
controls_and_missing_evidence.missing_condition_control: Missing water/temperature/recipe data must remain unassessed, not negative.
missing_method_fields: individual byproduct quantification and detection limits
controls_and_missing_evidence.local_route_conditions: Generated routes do not supply these observed process variables.

decision: Do not implement an automatic byproduct-formation or quantity rule from abstract-only evidence. Preserve this narrow comparison for the report and obtain matched full-method evidence before a supported chemistry module is added.
limitations: Candidate structure is not proof of actual formation or patient exposure.
A reported 99% product purity is not a transferable 1% byproduct quantity.
No yield-derived toxic threshold, universal byproduct model, or safety conclusion is produced.
